Our manifesto

Set a sketchbook on a desk and you can still see the person sitting across from you. Open a computer and a little wall goes up. We began with a question. What if you could open your work and keep that view?

That question gave ANTIK its glass. A drawing can hang in front of you while the pencil, the paper, and the hand that made the first mark stay in sight.

Its name comes from the Antikythera mechanism. Over two thousand years ago, craftspeople cut gears in bronze to follow the movements of the sky. Their work still invites a closer look. We want to make a computer worth keeping, repairing, and eventually putting into someone else’s hands.

Lux Vitae means “light of life.” Our star takes its shape from the first light over Earth’s horizon.

“A machine of light and glass, built with the craftsman’s reverence, meant to be kept, maintained, and passed down rather than discarded.”

William Bennett, Origins of ANTIK
